assessment: Chronic pain is a major health issue that is notably lacking pharmacological, non-opioid treatment options. The authors of this manuscript have deployed a powerful combination of experimental and computational tools to optimize the binding and selectivity of a series of peptide toxins derived from the toxin Protoxin II. The authors succeed in obtaining a peptide with improved selectivity and affinity for the human sodium channel Nav1.7, which is a major player in pain transmission and generation. This strategy represents a major advance on the road to obtaining specific peptide inhibitors for the treatment of chronic pain.
